newsitem.title: USA: Boston Chicken not satisfied with sales.
newsitem.headline: Boston Chicken not satisfied with sales.

text.p: Boston Chicken Inc said Thursday it was "not satisfied" with current sales momentum in its Boston Market stores, sending the stock reeling in early trading.
The stock fell nearly 10 percent in very heavy early trading, falling 1-1/2 to 16-5/8 with over two million shares traded.

President and chief executive Larry Zwain has resigned but will remain on the board. Scott Beck and Saad Nadhir will share the office of chairman and Beck retains his position as chief executive. Formerly, Beck was chairman and CEO and Nadhir was vice chairman. The two will refocus on the core business, home meal replacement.
"The issue is that we've begun to see this lunch-driven discounting negatively impact our dinner sales," said Beck in a release.
Nadhir will spearhead a plan to expand market share in the home meal replacement area, including testing sales of chilled ready-to-heat meals during the third quarter.

Boston Market also said it has built up "too many layers" over the past five years and is working on cutting duplications between area developers and a company support center, which should reduce overhead costs. It also plans to streamline certain administrative functions.
The changes will not involve employees at the store level, or Einstein/Noah Bagel Corp, which is 53 percent owned by Boston Chicken.
The shares touched a new low of 16, a level it has not seen since late 1994.
